evals.name: attend-queue-one-merged-view-escalations-ratify-intake
evals.prompt:
/work-items:attend-queue

The repository has: two open items wearing the human-gated role label, one with a machine-marked work-items:escalation comment (a worker question) and one parked by the operator with no marker; one item whose escalation marker carries kind=ratify-c3; four untriaged items (two unlabeled, one with the raw marker, one status:needs-info where the reporter just replied). The binding remaps human-gated to blocked-on-human.
evals.expected_output: One merged attention view, oldest first, rows tagged [escalated], [ratify], and [intake]. The human-gated role resolves from config.role_labels to blocked-on-human and is never compared as the needs-human literal. Only the item with the machine-marked escalation comment appears as [escalated] — the parked item wearing the same label but no marker is excluded, because the marker (not the label) discriminates escalated from parked. The ratify-c3 item appears as [ratify]. The [intake] rows come from composing /work-items:triage's attention view (unlabeled, raw marker, needs-info-with-reply buckets), not from a re-derived bucket definition. Ratifications are worked first at equal age since they unblock the waiting worker loop.
expectations: Builds ONE merged view containing escalations, ratifications, and untriaged intake — not separate disconnected reports
Resolves the human-gated role from config.role_labels (blocked-on-human) and never queries or compares the needs-human default literal after the remap
Includes as [escalated] only items carrying BOTH the human-gated role label AND a machine-marked work-items:escalation comment; excludes the operator-parked item that has the label but no marker
Tags the kind=ratify-c3 item as [ratify] and prioritizes ratify rows at equal age
Sources [intake] rows by composing /work-items:triage's attention view rather than re-deriving its buckets

evals.name: attend-queue-answers-write-back-ratify-and-flip
evals.prompt:
/work-items:attend-queue

The operator works three rows: an [escalated] item where the worker asked which of two API shapes to keep; a [ratify] row for a C3 bug-fix admission; and an [intake] bug report. The operator answers the API question, ratifies the C3 admission, and directs triage on the bug.
evals.expected_output: For the escalated row, the decision is driven via /planning:interview when the planning plugin is installed (inline focused questions, one at a time, as the documented fallback) and the answer is written back as an issue comment on the item — the decision lives on the tracker, not only in the session — after which the item is flipped: the autonomous-eligible role label applied and the human-gated role label removed in the same edit, both resolved from config.role_labels. For the ratify row, the ratification is recorded as a reply comment and the same single-edit flip applies; the item re-enters the worker loop's frontier — this lane never dispatches or executes it. For the intake row, /work-items:triage runs under its interactive direction gate: recommendation first, mutation only after the operator's direction. Agent-authored comments carry the AI disclaimer.
expectations: Uses /planning:interview behind an installed-ness gate with the inline focused-questions fallback documented at the site
Writes the operator's answer back as an issue comment on the escalated item rather than leaving the decision only in the session
Flips items in ONE edit that applies the autonomous-eligible role and removes the human-gated role, both resolved from config.role_labels — never leaves an item wearing both roles
Records the C3 ratification as a reply comment and returns the item to the frontier without executing or dispatching it from this lane
Runs intake triage through /work-items:triage's interactive direction gate — recommend, wait for direction, then mutate
Prefixes agent-authored comments with the AI disclaimer
Never merges a PR and never executes a work item from this lane

evals.name: attend-queue-briefs-before-asking-each-row
evals.prompt:
/work-items:attend-queue

The operator works two rows back to back in the same pass: an [escalated] item asking which of two retry strategies to keep, then a [ratify] row for a C3 admission on a completely different item.
evals.expected_output: Before posing the escalated question, restates which item it concerns (number + one-line title), the decision being asked (which retry strategy to keep), and the consequence of each option. Moving to the very next row, the same restatement happens again for the ratify prompt — the operator's context from the escalated row is never assumed to carry over, even though it was the immediately preceding row in the same pass. Neither restatement is dropped or abbreviated for brevity.
expectations: Restates item identity, the decision being asked, and the consequence of each option before posing the escalated question
Repeats the same full restatement for the very next row (the ratify prompt) rather than assuming context carries over from the prior row in the same pass
Does not compress or drop the restatement for either row even under a terse output style
Still performs the row's underlying mechanics (interview/write-back for escalated, ratify-or-decline recording for ratify) after the restatement — the brief precedes the ask, it does not replace it
